explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM judges (GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-72B) with human evaluators on 1,405 Vi-DROP instances, reporting agreement rates and analyzing disagreements

prompts.notes: Full evaluation prompts provided in Appendix C, including detailed 7-criteria rubric and scoring rules for Vi-SQuAD and Vi-DROP tasks

human_eval_details.num_evaluators: Not specified (multiple reviewers per data point)

guidelines.notes: Describes multi-layered quality assurance process with three independent reviewers per data point, but specific human evaluation guidelines for validation subset not detailed

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on 1,405 Vi-DROP questions comparing LLM judgments with human evaluations

quantitative_scores.notes: High correlation between two LLM judges

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM judges show high accuracy and strong correlation with human evaluations for short-text comparison tasks, but dialog evaluation remains challenging with low human agreement (0.49)

criteria_mapping.notes: Human evaluation focuses on semantic accuracy comparison against ground truth, while LLM judges use comprehensive 7-criteria rubric adapted from TencentLLMEval
